views.name: jobs_with_applied
views.definition:
SELECT j.id,
    j.company,
    j.title,
    j.url,
    j.location,
    j.description,
    j.is_active,
    j.first_seen_at,
    j.last_seen_at,
    j.scraped_at,
    j.source_payload,
    j.ats,
    j.posted_at,
    j.closed_at,
    j.description_raw,
    j.description_clean,
    a.id IS NOT NULL AS is_applied,
    a.status AS applied_status,
    a.applied_at
   FROM jobs j
     LEFT JOIN applications a ON a.company = j.company AND a.job_url = j.url;

views.name: robotics_jobs_with_applied
views.definition:

    j.company,
    j.title,

views.name: team_jobs_with_applied
views.definition:
SELECT j.id,
    j.league,
    j.team,
    j.company,
    j.title,
    j.url,
    j.location,
    j.description,
    j.platform,
    j.ats,
    j.posted_at,
    j.first_seen_at,
    j.last_seen_at,
    j.scraped_at,
    j.is_active,
    j.closed_at,
    j.logo_url,
    j.source_id,
    j.salary,
    j.detail_status,
    j.detail_checked_at,
    a.id IS NOT NULL AS is_applied,
    a.status AS applied_status,
    a.applied_at
   FROM team_jobs j
     LEFT JOIN team_applications a ON a.job_url = j.url AND a.company = j.company AND a.user_id = auth.uid();

triggers.name: team_keep_first_seen
triggers.definition: CREATE TRIGGER team_keep_first_seen BEFORE UPDATE ON public.team_jobs FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION team_keep_first_seen()
triggers.function_definition:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.team_keep_first_seen()
 RETURNS trigger
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $function$
begin new.first_seen_at=old.first_seen_at; return new; end; $function$
